chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from Zur'ah from Samaan, who said:
I asked him about two men who share a female slave, and they married her to another man. Then one of the men bought one of the two shares. He said: 'She became prohibited (for marriage) to him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a shared female slave who is married to another man when one owner buys the other's share?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that if two co-owners of a female slave marry her to a third party, and one subsequently purchases the other's share, she becomes permanently prohibited (haram) to that buyer. This ruling highlights the principle of *tamalluk* (possession) in Shia jurisprudence, where acquiring full ownership through the consolidation of shares establishes the marital bond's exclusivity, preventing further marriage to others while maintaining the prohibition on the buyer marrying her if the specific conditions of 'buying the share' imply a change in the nature of possession relative to the existing marriage contract.
